\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial-time approximation for Max-Cut]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.goemans_williamson_polyTime}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.goemans_williamson_polyTime}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.cutValue, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.gwConstant, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.optimum, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.maxCutGraph, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.parseMaxCut, BooleanAnalysis.expect, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Turing.pairEncode}
For every real $\\eta>0$, there is a polynomial-time computable map $A$ from bit strings
to bit strings and there are natural numbers $C,k$ with the following property. Whenever
a bit string parses as a nonempty list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers, encode
each pair in $E$ as an edge of a weighted graph, giving each ordered pair $(u,v)$ weight
equal to the total number of occurrences of $(u,v)$ and $(v,u)$ in $E$, divided by twice
the length of $E$. The expected cut value of this graph, using the Boolean assignment
whose value at vertex $v$ is the $v$th output bit of $A$ on the encoding of the input
bit string paired with a uniformly random bit string of length
$C(\\lvert\\text{bits}\\rvert+1)^k$ (and using false when that output has no $v$th bit),
is at least the Goemans–Williamson constant times the graph’s maximum cut value minus
$\\eta$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Thresholded polynomial-time approximation]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.goemans_williamson_threshold_polyTime}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.goemans_williamson_threshold_polyTime}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.cutValue, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.gwAngle, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.MaxCut.sdpOptimum, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.maxCutGraph, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.UniqueGames.parseMaxCut, BooleanAnalysis.expect, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Turing.pairEncode}
For every real $\\eta>0$, there is a polynomial-time computable map $A$ from bit strings
to bit strings and there are natural numbers $C,k$ with the following property. Whenever
a bit string parses as a nonempty list $E$ of ordered pairs of natural numbers, form the
weighted graph that assigns each ordered pair $(u,v)$ weight equal to the total number
of occurrences of $(u,v)$ and $(v,u)$ in $E$, divided by twice the length of $E$. For
every angle $\\theta$ between the Goemans–Williamson angle and $\\pi$, inclusive, such
that $(1-\\cos\\theta)/2$ is at most this graph’s SDP optimum, the expected cut value of
the graph under the Boolean assignment given by the $v$th output bit of $A$ on the
encoding of the input paired with a uniformly random bit string of length
$C(\\lvert\\text{bits}\\rvert+1)^k$ (using false if the output has no $v$th bit) is at
least $\\theta/\\pi-\\eta$.
\end{theorem}
